newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says money growth slows down in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says money growth slows down in Nov.

text.p: The growth in Philippine money supply, as measured by base money and domestic liquidity, slowed down in November, the Central Bank said on Thursday.
The bank, in a statement, said the annual growth in base money decelerated to 10.2 percent last month from 13.6 percent in October.
Domestic liquidity, or M3, slowed down to 22 percent from 25.8 percent at the start of the year.
Base money includes money in circulation, reserve balances and government securities deposited with the Central Bank and the aggregate reserve deficiencies of banks.
The base money level was 40 billion pesos below the programmed level set by the International Monetary Fund, the Central Bank added.
Domestic liquidity includes base money plus the deposits and deposit substitutes with banks.
This level was also 40 billion pesos below the ceiling set by the IMF.
Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson attributed the slowdown in monetary growth to the bank's active open market operations.
The bank issues short and long-termed reverse repos and special series Treasury bills to mop up excess liquidity in the market.
Singson added that the limited growth in money supply would made the full year inflation target of 8.5 percent easily attainable. The average inflation for the first 11 months was at 8.7 percent.
He said the December inflation should be "at most 6.3 percent."
"To secure the continued deceleration of inflation ... the monetary authorities will sustain monetary discipline as shown in previous months," the statement added.
